name: Jellyio Streams
description: Stream Stremio-addon content from your self-hosted AIOStreams instance. The plugin generates a Jellyfin library (.strm files plus nfo metadata) with a Stremio-like stream picker: each resolved stream becomes a selectable version of the item. Includes catalog sync, search & add, and a scheduled refresh task.
overview: Stream Stremio-addon content from a self-hosted AIOStreams instance

versions.changelog: New: dedicated 'Jellyio Streams' search page in the dashboard sidebar. Search AIOStreams for a movie or series, add it, and it appears in your library - no catalog sync needed, so your library only contains what you add. The page also lists what is already in the library folder, and /AIOStreams/Library reports the on-disk titles.

Sync now shows live progress instead of appearing to hang: the sync reports the current catalog/title, percent, and elapsed time, and the settings page polls the status endpoint while it runs. The sync button is disabled while a sync is active. A full sync makes hundreds of addon requests (every title, and with MaxEpisodesPerSeries=0 every episode of every series), so it can legitimately take many minutes; cap Episodes per series or Titles per catalog to speed it up.

"Test connection" now saves the addon URL first (the 400 "addon URL is not configured" was almost always a URL that was typed but never saved). The settings page status box now shows the server-side plugin version and whether the addon URL is configured, and the 400 message reports the running plugin version so an outdated install is obvious. Jellyfin must be restarted after updating.

Fix the settings page losing the addon URL. Jellyfin's plugin config endpoint deserializes case-sensitively with no naming policy, so it returns PascalCase and only accepts PascalCase: the page's camelCase reads always yielded undefined, the form loaded blank, and the next Save posted those blanks back and reset the stored configuration. The page now reads either casing, scopes every lookup to the visible page instance (the dashboard caches old copies with duplicate element ids), refuses to save empty settings when the config could not be read, and re-reads the configuration after saving to confirm what the server actually stored.
Fix: read camelCase JSON from API responses, write PascalCase for config save (Jellyfin's config deserializer has no naming policy). Handle HTTP 204 from config endpoint as save success.
Fix: config page now reads and writes camelCase JSON keys matching Jellyfin's API serializer. This was the root cause of Save appearing to do nothing.
API endpoints return proper 400 responses with readable messages instead of unhandled 500s; config page now shows HTTP status and server error text instead of '[object Response]'.

Harden config page: errors now display on the page instead of failing silently; Save builds the config from the form directly (works even if initial load failed); defensive ApiClient/Dashboard checks; global error hook.

Fix: configuration page rewritten in plain HTML. Jellyfin 10.11 no longer processes emby components (data-require) and never fires DOMContentLoaded on injected plugin pages, so the previous page showed raw icon text ('saveSave') and its buttons did nothing.
Fix: scheduled task trigger now correctly uses IntervalTrigger type. Fixes a startup crash ('Info did not contain a TimeOfDayTicks') that prevented Jellyfin from starting when the plugin was enabled.
Initial release: catalog sync, search & add, version-based stream selection, scheduled refresh.
